utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Various matters left over from yesterday. Mr. Nice, while it's in my mind, the matter you -- which was referred to yesterday, and I asked you perhaps to look into it, have you had any further consideration?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I've had a few further thoughts. I realised myself this morning that I omitted to provide anything in writing, which I'd effectively agreed to do yesterday. I don't actually know that even if I had remembered yesterday afternoon I would have had the resources, but if I can come back to that later this morning, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But there is something of a precedent in Blaskic, and I'll try and get chapter and verse of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour has another point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Milosevic wants to raise some matters

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I raise two points while I'm on my feet, one to which he may want to respond. In relation to yesterday's witness K5, criminal record matters were raised with him. He denied them all. If the accused has records of the courts concerned - and he was giving numbers - then it would be administratively helpful and probably proper for them to be provided to us through the Registry for us to consider, and I'd invite him to make those available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The second point is in relation to the process whereby witnesses are subject to 92 bis'ing at Court. I'm not sure that I like the shorthand advantageous though it is, to say one "bises" a witness, but I'm afraid that's what we do say that. The long form is too long, the short form is too short. That process, at court, is said by the Registry to require five full working days of notice to them by us before an appointment can be made. It's effectively impossible for us to give precise notice for various witnesses and there are, I think, two or it may be even three witness here at court today, or coming today, for whom short-term 92 bis process would be desirable and would save time. I am don't know if the court is going to be able to intercede on our behalf or help, but that's a problem we're facing. As we were discussing it this morning, one of my colleagues helpfully said, well, maybe the answer is simply effectively to bis at Court, that is, the witness comes here and is allowed to say, yes, I have got through this statement and that statement, and it is true. It's something we did, I think, once in Kordic when the Court was very pressed for time. We did it then actually not with a statement but with a summary, but of course, the trouble with doing that as a shorthand method is it then obviates the need altogether for the 92 bis procedure and it might be thought to be contrary to the purpose of the Rules. But those are a couple of problems we are facing. And so far as K12 is concerned, I think he's outstanding for decision as to whether he's properly subject to the 92 bis procedure. If you haven't had him, then that -- I'm giving you incorrect information. I understand we're waiting for a decision on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have to tell you, I don't recollect K12.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Let me check with Ms. Graham, rather than take time, when it was provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we've had that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Our recollection is last Thursday, but we'll check and provide again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But while we're dealing with it, it may be convenient. We've had the statement of Mr. Hendrie.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The statement has been served on us and although it may be he has not been through the procedure, it would appear at least prima facie that he is a witness to whom 92 bis could apply, subject to any submissions which are made by anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful. He's certainly one of the ones for whom short-term bis'ing process would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps I could refer to the Registry and ask them if it's at all possible to make facilities in this particular case although we understand, of course, they are pressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we turn to Mr. Milosevic's exhibits, there are some matters I need to do. I need to give a ruling in the case of Mr. Kelly, but before I do that, we ought to deal with some practical matters. Tomorrow, the accused has his dental appointment, so we won't start until 10.30. Is General Maisonneuve here or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He will be. He will be here, yes. Incidentally, in relation to Mr. Kelly, although I'd said that you'd had the jurisprudence on earlier occasions, I was hoping to make further argument to you about the scope of his evidence, and indeed I had planned to take him through the non-controversial -- if there is any controversy about his evidence, the non-controversial part of his evidence first in order to explain, if there's any doubt about it, why his report in full should be admitted, and I'd like the opportunity to do that. It won't waste any time because the non-controversial part, geography and matters of that sort, will be -- will have to be before you in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So you -- you would propose to call him and then make the application.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Go through the evidence of geography and the bare bones of what his investigation was, and then make the application after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll deal with it in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But going back to General Maisonneuve, he's here Wednesday, and he can be available for some days, can he, or what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think he can only be available for the one day. The Chamber indicated last week that, subject to argument, parts of his statement might be apt for the 92 bis procedure, and Mr. Ryneveld, who will be taking him, has identified what he believes to be those that are and those that are not. That, therefore, would mean that his evidence will be shorter in duration than otherwise. We would hope that he can be completed in the day. Whether he has flexibility to extend his stay, I don't at the moment know, but he came on an earlier occasion and it was certainly difficult to timetable him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Obviously he should be called tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He may have to be interposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. We're working on the basis of wrapping other evidence around his timetabled appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Tomorrow will be 10.30, so it will be a short day in any event, but we'll have to see how that day transpires. While we're dealing with the timetable, Friday will also be a short day, 9.00 until 11.45. We have to deal with argument in another case later in the day that day. But we should, that morning, deal with the -- your application to vary our January order, which means we ought to be reviewing the case as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Arrangements are being made so that can be dealt with expeditiously on Friday, but I think a lot of topics are going to arise. I've got my own list of issues to raise with you which will affect evidence in this and the other cases or may start the process of affecting the evidence in this and the other parts of the case, as well as responding to your particular concerns in the Scheduling Order, so I hope there will be enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you give us notice of that so we can consider how long to allow for it? But we will have to adjourn this case at 11.45 on Friday. Unless there are any other matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you were dealing last night with -- or, rather, yesterday afternoon when we adjourned, with some exhibits that you wanted admitted. Could you tell us briefly what they are, and we'll consider them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the briefest possible terms. In connection with Mr. Merovci's testimony. Point 1 I have is the question that has to do with the LDK. It was supposed to take part in the elections in Serbia, but their assessment was that they would not win more than 15 seats in parliament, which is what they had then. That was my assertion, and I am submitting this to you by way of an exhibit or, rather, the material that the opposing party had actually made public or, rather, disclosed. It says, Rugova about the platform of the Democratic League of Kosovo. The number 030 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker will have to slow down when giving numbers. Could the numbers please be repeated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're asked by the interpreters, could you repeat the numbers slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of the document, the Serbian version, is 03037052, paragraph 3, and the last one. And the English version is K0214130. So it is 021410, paragraph 3. And I'm submitting only the Serbian version to you. That is one point I wish to make. Number 2, as for Witness Merovci and Rugova and his party, that they -- they said that I told the international community that there would be a radicalisation in Kosovo at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we don't want to go over it all again, with respect. I don't --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want you to link all of this up together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can do that. We've heard the evidence, and we can see whether it's relevant or not. Now, why can't you hand in both the Serb and the English versions of the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, no, I only have the version in Serbian. But you will find the English version because I've given you the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you hand in the documents now, we can then consider them. But we can't really waste a lot of time going over them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are not considering anything. I'm just giving you the number of documents. This has to do with the warning concerning radicalisation. The Serb version is 03036489, paragraphs 3 and 8, and the English version is K0214097, paragraphs 2 and 7, and I'm submitting both the English and Serbian versions to you. So that's a different matter altogether. Now, point number 3. In relation to the question that had to do with the green light for union with Albania, I am submitting yet again another paper, 03036366, paragraphs 4 and 5. And the English version is 214092, paragraphs 4 and 5, and I'm submitting both the Serbian and the English versions to you. Point number 4, the plan for a secession, for the secession of Kosovo. Evidence of that concerning international protection, the Serb version is 03036508, paragraph 5, and the English version is K0214118, paragraph 4. I am submitting both the English and Serbian versions to you. Point number 5. As for the attitude of their party towards the KLA as extremists, I'm submitting to you the Serb version, number 03036356, and the English version is 00805327, and I'm submitting both the English and Serbian versions to you. So that's that. Last but not least, point number 6, the question that had to do with the Hill plan and the draft related to Kosovo. The Serb version is 03036534, and the English version is 00805325 and 0080526. So I'm submitting that to you as well. So that would be it. And I haven't got anything left on that score, but Mr. Ognjanovic is going to submit a cassette as well, the one that you requested, the one that I quoted. It would have been submitted to you earlier, but the explanation he got, my associate, when he wanted to come and bring it to me on Friday, was that he could not bring a cassette in, into the prison, that is, because this was not approved by the Registrar. And the explanation was that for every cassette that is brought to me to prison, there has to be an individual approval given by the Registrar. So could you please have that clarified. If I have the right to have my associates bring me documents related to this case, I should think that it also has to do with cassettes as well. And then if he says the previous day that he is going to bring legal documents, that is to say documents, cassettes, et cetera, could you please look into this and see whether each and every time every tape has to be submitted to the Registrar and then does this communication with prison have to go through the Registrar? That would be about it. As you can see, I've been quite brief. You have all six exhibits here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us have the exhibits. If the usher would collect them, please. If the registrar would hand them up. And we'll also ask her to look into the matter of the cassette too, if you would. Very well. We will hand these now to the Prosecution to look at and see if there's any objection. Otherwise, they will be exhibited. Mr. Milosevic, the other point you were asked about was the question of court records referred to yesterday. You asked about some court records. You referred to them. Do you have any copies of those records available for the Court so we can check them out?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the numbers, the ones that I mentioned. I haven't got the copies of the court records, but they can be obtained, because the court records from Urosevac are actually kept at the court in Nis. So the court authorities of Yugoslavia have got them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Nice, if you could pursue that matter, obviously it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. We will pursue that. It will, of course, take some time. And there's no guarantee of success. It depends on the cooperation of the authorities. As to these exhibits, it's probably safer if I hand back the Serb versions now than run the risk of them getting lost in our paperwork. If the Registry could hang on to them. We'll check the English versions when we've dug them out and will respond whether we have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be convenient then for them to have exhibit numbers, at least for identification at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think that would be sensible. I've still got some outstanding issues on newspaper articles to come back on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It may be convenient if we call the evidence now while the registrar decides on numbers for those and in due course we can come back to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apparently the English versions were there already, so I'm wrong, I can work on those documents and will work on them today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the registrar have them for the moment and give them numbers and then you can have them and see if there's any objection. Now, can we go on with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: William Robert Fulton. Madam Registrar, I will be using with this witness Exhibit 166 is the binder for Suva Reka, and I would ask, if possible, the witness be given one set of the binders. It's the second binder of Suva Reka. And also Exhibit 167 is the Meja binder. And Your Honours, I also ask permission for the witness to refer to his notes. I think you have a copy of his summary and he is an investigator who was in Belgrade and he participated in monitoring the mass graves, the exhumations, and he took extensive notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, he can refer to his notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you give us your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: William Robert Fulton.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, I will ask you to pause between questions and answers in order for the interpreters to do their work. Mr. Fulton, you were a police officer holding the rank of detective sergeant in the Royal Ulster Constabulary, now renamed the Police Service of Northern Ireland, for 23 years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Have you been involved in organisational training in identification of dead bodies in major disasters?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. I was a co-author of the RUC's Contingency Plan on the Recovery and Identification of Dead Bodies at Major Disasters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: You were seconded to the British forensic team to work in Kosovo in September and October 1999, and again in 2000 for the exhumation work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: You have been currently working as an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor since May 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, on June 6, 2001, you were assigned to work in the field office in Belgrade. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Who assigned you to this work, and what was your work over there?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I was assigned to go to Belgrade by my team leader, Mr. Kevin Curtis, to monitor the exhumation process that was scheduled to start within the boundaries of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: How many sites in total have you monitored?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: During my time in Serbia, there was four sites. However, I was involved in the monitoring of two of them. However, I did visit all four sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you -- can you name the sites for the Court?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was two in an area called Batajnica, one in Petrovo Selo -- actually, two in Petrovo Selo, both very, very close to one another, and the other in the area of Lake Perucac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can I have the witness shown this map. The accused and the amici, they have already, and I have copies for the Court here. It is a map of Serbia where is shown the location of the mass graves and exhumation sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Witness, with the help of the map when you have it, can you show to the Court the location, the exact location of the sites?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. The first site I attended was on the outskirts of Belgrade, approximately 20 kilometres, in Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you please point to the location of the site.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This is Batajnica. The next site that I attended was the one in Petrovo Selo, which is here. Of course there was two in Batajnica. And, finally, there was one in Lake Perucac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The Prosecution submits the map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 172.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, these exhumations relate to mass graves that have been recently discovered in Serbia. Can you please tell the Court how did these mass graves came to be discovered and who was in charge of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Information received at the Office of the Prosecutor, primarily from media reports, there was an investigation carried out as a result of a -- what's known as the freezer lorry in the Danube, quite close to a village called Tekija, that was investigated by Captain Dragan Karleusa. He's deputy chief of police of the MUP. And it was alleged to contain bodies of victims who had been killed in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you explain, if you can, with more details how was this investigation in the lorry or if you know that? When was this lorry discovered and when the investigation started?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: My understanding is that the lorry was discovered in the River Danube in April of 1999. The investigation initiated by the MUP would have been sometime later, certainly within 2001, which in turn led to the identification of an area, the first Batajnica site, that was selected for exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And as a result of this investigation, it was believed that these mass graves contained bodies of persons killed in Kosovo during the conflict; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That was the indication, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And has the Office of the Prosecutor established any connection between the bodies and the victims named in the second amended indictment later on?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: As a result of the exhumation that was carried out by the experts from the Institute of Forensic Science in Belgrade who carried out the duty at the exhumation site of Batajnica 1, a number of items of identification were recovered that would tend to indicate that these identifications belonged and referred to people from Kosovo and principally from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Who carried out the exhumations, all the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The exhumations were performed, as I say, by members of the Belgrade Institute of Forensic Medicine under the direct -- the person in charge was Professor Dusan Dunjic and members of his staff involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Have they finished all the exhumation work?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: My understanding is that all the -- all sites were identified by Captain Karleusa. On the second Batajnica site, there is still two more mass graves to be exhumed there. They have not been started as of -- to date.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And has the Office of the Prosecutor received all the reports, preliminary or final, of the exhumations that have been already concluded?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecutor has received, following an official request, the complete forensic reports concerning the first Batajnica site and the photographs that led to that. All other sites, although requested, have not been forwarded to us as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: But the Office of the Prosecutor has requested to obtain these reports?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Were you assigned to monitor the exhumation process while they were being performed?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And can you describe your role.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: My role was purely non-interventionist. I was there simply to monitor the procedures of how the exhumation process took place, the evidential recording, and anything of any significance that was found at the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: All the information gathered concerning the first site on Batajnica, Batajnica, is contained in a binder that you compiled with other members of the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can I have the witness shown or given Suva Reka, the second binder of Suva Reka, Exhibit 166.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Batajnica was the first site that you attended. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Batajnica 1 was the first site, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: In the binder, in tab 29, you have a photo of the exhumation of the site. Can you show the photo to the Court.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: On this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you can help the witness to put the photo on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: That is the site of the exhumation in Batajnica?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the -- all these photographs were taken by the crime tech, technician, who was working with the exhumation team, and these number of photographs show the topography of the area at the start of the exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Where was the exact location of this site? Was it in the outskirts of Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the outskirts of Belgrade, as I referred to, in Batajnica. Directly behind or to the left of this photograph is the boundary fence of a special anti-terrorist unit, the SAJ, and their firing range only a matter of metres to the left. This actually abuts the perimeter fence of this complex and a VJ complex.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Who provided you with information about this mass grave?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The information that was obtained through the police investigation was passed to Belgrade District Court where an investigating judge was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The investigating judge for the first Batajnica site was Goran Cavlina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And the forensic team was composed of how many people?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There were a number pathologists who did a rotation. There was anthropologists, archaeologists, and assistants who helped in the actual labour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And when did the exhumations take place and what is the period of time that you attended the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I attended the exhumations from the 10th of June until the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Were you the only observer?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: No. There are several other observers from Humanitarian Law Centre, OSCE, ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: During the course of the exhumations, were any bodies recovered? And if any, how many?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The indications that were given to me were that the total number of bodies numbered between 36 -- well, at least 36 to 38 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: How many male, female, and children?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There were 14 females, 13 men, nine children, and one foetus.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Were identification items such as documents or clothing also recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. A number of those items were recovered, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And you were -- were you present at the site when these documents were recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were the details contained in the documents given to you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make a pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: My apology.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So -- and did you also get copies of these documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: When the official request was agreed to, we were supplied with photographic recordings of all the identification documents that were recovered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And while you were on the site and the documents were being recovered, what did you do with the information that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The information was passed to me by members of the team. Whenever I was in receipt of that information, I passed it to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And did the members of the Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague, did they check their records in order to determine if any of the details matched to the victims of the crimes investigated by our office?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what was established?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Indications were that these people and the identification -- sorry, the identification documents that were recovered referred to people who had been killed in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And from all the documents recovered, how many of them matched with the details from the victims of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Of the -- sorry. I can't remember how many now. I think it was -- it was nine documents recovered. And eight of those referred to people who had been killed within Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you later obtained copies of photographs and also forensic reports?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: When did you obtain that and from whom?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Whenever the forensic team had completed their reports, they were handed in to Belgrade District Court. The copies of the forensic reports and the photographs were obtained from the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And are they compiled in the binder that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Are they -- the forensic reports are compiled on the tabs 34 to 38 and 41; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Sorry, what was the numbers again? 38, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: 34 to 38 and 41.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. These are the forensic reports as compiled by -- and signed by Professor Dunjic and members of his forensic team.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And they relate to the nine identification items?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, there are considerably more forensic reports. However, these are the ones that refer to the identification documents and the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And the photographs? Are they contained under tabs 19 to 27?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, they are, Your Honours. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Using the photographs, can you please tell the court the names of the individuals identified and what kind of documents or identification items were recovered that allowed the identification? Maybe you can refer to the index, if you have it.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Shall I show this one? Because it is in Latin, it shows quite clearly the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Put that on, if you would, Mr. Fulton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph is a licna karta, which is an identification document, is associated with body PA09, and it shows the details and the name of Afrim Berisha from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is Afrim Berisha one of the victims listed in Attachment K of the second amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: What is the name of the second victim?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The second victim is Nexhmedin Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: All the photos contained in tab 20?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: They refer to the identification of Nexhmedin Berisha? And what was the item recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That is a licna karta.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The next victim?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The next identification document is a driving licence in the name of -- I was given initially as Morina Miftar. However, it since has been referred to -- because there is a lot of degradation of these documents. Some were clearly better than others because of the body fluids, there was evidence of burning. I considered it disruption. So some of the details are, primarily in this one, are perhaps not as clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: This person is not listed in Attachment K, but is this person from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. Indications are that this person is from the Suva Reka municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you. The next person is Hamdi Berisha. Is tab 22.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And where was the document found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This one is a licna karta.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to do it in a more expeditious way, Your Honours want me to go one by one and see all the documents, or I just can refer to the tab and lay it on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't have to see the documents but just refer to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: To them. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So, Mr. Fulton, can you just refer to the name and what was the document found and the tab that can be located. You can use the index. So the next person would be Hamdi Berisha. Where was the document? Excuse me, we passed already Hamdi Berisha. It is Fatmira Berisha.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Fatmira Berisha, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Where was the document found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This document was found in items of loose clothing and it contains a licna karta which relates to the name of Fatmira Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And Hamdi Berisha and Fatmira Berisha are listed in Attachment K of the amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: You also have a health care on the name of Hamdi Berisha?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. I've been told that this is a health insurance card in the name of Hamdi Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: It's the same Hamdi Berisha as was in the licna karta or are different persons?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I can't determine that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The next would be Vesel Berisha.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. There was a considerable amount of documents recovered with this body. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And in tab 25?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Hasan Bytyqi?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This is a licna karta and a driving licence in the name of Hasan Bytyci. There is also a vehicle registration licence in the name of Zoga Mehdin.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what is the tab? 26?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Twenty-six.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is this person from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The next one would be Musli Berisha?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Twenty-seven. Yes, licna karta in the name of Musli Berisha. These last number of items apart from the first two were found in items of loose clothing of which there was a considerable amount.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: I think we covered all the nine. Mr. Fulton, was there another attempt to identify the bodies and remains recovered from this site using other means of identification?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Ordinarily, it is possible to identify bodies comparing antemortem data, which is data pre-death, to the post-mortem data that is recovered at the exhumation. Because of the nature of the bodies, where there was considerable fracturing and commingling and burning, it was clear that we would have to use the facility that could be afforded by DNA process.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And did Belgrade -- did Belgrade have facilities such like that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It was established that Belgrade did not have the facility to carry out such a DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So what was done?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: A facility was agreed by a DNA facility in Madrid who would process the samples that were obtained from Batajnica 1 for the purpose of DNA identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So on 21st November, 2001, you accompanied Professor Dunjic to Madrid?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: To the Instituto Nacional do Toxicologia.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And has a preliminary report already been prepared?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic took the samples and delivered them to the institute in Madrid, and they -- and a preliminary result has been supplied by this institute.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And how did the samples from the relatives of the victims, how did they -- how did they -- how were they gathered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was blood samples from the remaining members of the families of people from Suva Reka were obtained from the institute -- or from the ICMT -- the ICMP, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And has the Office of the Prosecutor received this preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, this report has been sent to the Office of the Prosecutor and to Professor Dunjic in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is this the report that is in tab 28?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what were the preliminary findings contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There are conclusions in this report from the Madrid institute that would indicate that there is a genetic link between a sample from body BA34 and BA52 to a blood sample that was obtained from the relatives of the victims from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And the photographs related to these two bodies are in tabs 31 and 32 of the binder?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Actually, in 30, 31, and 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And has the Office of the Prosecutor also received the forensic report related to these two bodies?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And are they in tabs 39 and 40?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: This analysis will be forwarded to the coordination centre for Kosovo for formal identification?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. The procedure over there is the formal identification has yet to be made. However, the -- it's a case of getting the DNA analysis, the antemortem data and the post-mortem data to make a formal identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: In the binder also there is a photo of the site after the job of the exhumation and the work was concluded. I believe this is in tab 33.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you please show the Court. What does the photo show?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's one photograph of the site at the conclusion and the exhumation of all the bodies and all associated materials. You will see that there is a number of railway sleepers that have been laid along the floor of the pit, and there's also evidence of burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what does this indicate?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The conclusions, it would appear that there has been an attempt to destroy the bodies by fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: I don't think we will be needing any more the binders. Mr. Fulton, all the information that the Office of the Prosecutor was asked regarding the work done in the three other exhumation sites are only your notes?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So the Office of the Prosecutor has not received yet the conclusions or the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I understand that the photographs and the forensic reports of the second Batajnica site that was performed by the Belgrade institute have been forwarded to the Court. However, we have not been receipt of them yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you give the exact location of the second exhumation site? It's also in Batajnica, but the exact location?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The second Batajnica site, as I referred to earlier, is a short distance from the first one. However, this one is actually -- was found to be inside the SAJ compound and on the firing range.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And again, who provided you with information?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This information was given by the courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And who was the investigative magistrate?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The investigating judge, appointed by the president of the court for the second Batajnica site was Judge Milan Dilparic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: How long did the exhumation last?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The exhumation from the second Batajnica site lasted from the 10th of July until the 15th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And did you attend during all at that time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: During the course of this exhumation, how many bodies, if any, were recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It has been indicated to me that the bodies of at least 269 people have been recovered from this one site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Were any of these bodies identified?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There's been no identification of any of those bodies so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were identification items - again such documents, clothing - also recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, there was a number of identification documents recovered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Do you remember how many?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was 11, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were you on the site when these documents were recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Were the details contained in these documents given to you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, the details were given to me by members of the team.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And again, what did you do with this information?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Whenever this information came into my possession, it was forwarded it the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And did the members of the Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague check their records in order to determine if any of the details matched to the victims of any of the crimes investigated by the office?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And which record was use by the members of the OTP in this case?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: They used the ICRC register.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can I have the witness shown the binder of Meja, Exhibit 167, tab 2. It's the list of missing persons from the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the Prosecutor kindly slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I will try my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: What is exactly this document, Mr. Fulton?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This records the details of persons who are -- have been reported missing as recorded by the ICRC and from where, and as much detail - father's name, date of birth - as is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what was established from all the documents recovered? How many of them matched with the details of people listed in the records?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Of identification documents recovered, I believe there was nine that referred to people who appear in the ICRC register.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: I believe it was eight.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Eight. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The first one would be Ali Bajrami. And if you can turn to page 61 of the ICRC list.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can the usher please help the witness to put the -- that page on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Ali Bajrami is listed as to have -- a person to have disappeared on the 27th of April, 1999, in Meja. What was the document found in the exhumation sites that connected to this person?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This was a licna karta in the name of Ali Bajrami, father's name Kadri.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The second person will be Simon Sokoli, and you can use page 67 this time and point to the court the location of the name. Can you point on the ELMO, please. And what was the document found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This again was a licna karta associated with body number 177 that was removed from this grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And did the details contained in the licna karta match with the details in the record of the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, they did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The other person would be Sezai Rama, and it's listed on page 66. I don't think we need to continue showing or putting on the ELMO. I would just ask you to refer to what was the -- what was the identification item found that allowed the match.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This was a health care card, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is it Shyt Hasanaj is listed in the record on page 63 what was the document found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This was a licna karta on body 221.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Krist Sokoli, ICRC list page 67.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This was a licna karta.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Gani Smajili, page 67 as well?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This again was a licna karta that was found on body 240.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Qun Bib Krasniqi. It's on page 60.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Sorry, what page again?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Page 60. This person is listed as missing from Korenica on the 27th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Sorry, could I have that name again?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Krasniqi Qun Bib.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The search does not really identify the missing person but identified, I believe, an individual named Ndue Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's right. Date of birth 12th of 1st, 1966. He has a father named Bibe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you clarify to the Court how this conclusion was reached?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Well, as you referred to, the search does not readily identify a missing person of this name, however, there is a close correlation between this individual and the one in the ICRC register on page 60.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So the conclusion was that Bibe Krasniqi probably is the father of the Ndue Krasniqi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yeah, there's a possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Brahim Gaxherri, and it's listed on page 62.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. This was a licna karta in the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: We have the eight people. Mr. Fulton, what was the third site that you visit?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was some overlap in a number of exhumations that were going on. The next site I attended was on the 27th of June, was the site of Petrovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And again the Office of the Prosecutor does not possess any -- any report or photographs from this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And while you were there, what did you monitor or observe?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: While the exhumation process was going on, I had only time for a short visit. However, information was passed to me. The exhumations at this site took place from the 24th of June until the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And how many bodies, if any, were recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: From the first site in Petrovo Selo, there were 16 bodies, all male; and from the second site, there were 57 bodies, seven of which were female.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were you able to ascertain any body or any documents? Were you given any documents of any of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I was informed that there had been a number of identification documents found from the first site. There was a document that referred to the names of three people by the name of Bytyqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what was done?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This in turn led to, I believe, to be from Kosovo. However, they were American citizens from Chicago, United States of America.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And was -- was any record checked in order to obtain this identification?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This information obtained through the -- at that time through the HRC, was able to lead us to indication that these were three brothers by the name of Agron, Mehmet, and Ylli.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were these three brothers reported as missing?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. They were reported missing to the ICRC from a prison near Nis on the 8th of July, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And what was recovered from the second site in Petrovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was five further documents recovered, three of which refer to people that correspond with details contained in the ICRC register.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Can you give us the three names and the document that was found and how -- where they report as missing?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was a licna karta in the name of Iljaz Muslija, who disappeared on the 1st of the 4th, 1999 from Izbica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is this person listed in the ICRC list page 40?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I have a reference number, which is SRB BLG 804238.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: What is the second person?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There is a licna karta found in an item of clothing in the name of Hysen Mehmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is this person reported disappeared?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: These details correspond to the ICRC register of a person who disappeared on the 24th of May 1999 from an unknown location.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Is this on page 85 of the ICRC list? You don't have the list with you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I don't have the list, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Page 85.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And -- and the third person?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Is a licna karta in the name of Nazmi Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And this person's reported missing from where and when?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This corresponds to ICRC register who disappeared on the 24th of 5th 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: It's on page 85 as well?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you. The last site, the fourth site in Lake Perucac, can you again give us the exact location and the exhumations took place -- when did they take place?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The exhumations took place from the 6th to the 14th of September, 2001 in Lake Perucac. It was given, such as BA or PS, it was given the identification moniker of D as the exhumation site itself was where the river Derventa went into the lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And how many bodies, if any, were recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: These bodies were again charred, skeletal, and had a considerable amount of fractures. The indications are that there was at least 48 bodies recovered from that exhumation site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And were any of the bodies identified?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There's been no identifications taken place on these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And documents or items?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It was brought to my attention two identification documents were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: What kind of documents and what are the contents or the details contained in these documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The first one is a licna karta that was found in an item of clothing in the name of Gezim Deva.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And who is this person and is recorded as missing somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This person is recorded as missing from Djakovica on the 31st of the 3rd 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is also part of the record of the ICRC list?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: It's page 37?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Thirty-seven, that's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And where was the second document recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: This was a driving licence in the name of Skeljzen Binishi, who refers to a person missing from Djakovica on the 31st of the 3rd 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And is this person also on page 37 of the ICRC list?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Here it is. I'm just having some difficulty honing in on it. Ah, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fulton, you followed the exhumation process throughout the period in Belgrade. According to your experience and identification of dead bodies, were the work conducted professionally and in an adequate manner?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no interpretation. Would you repeat that, please, Mr. Milosevic. It doesn't seem to have been translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I'll repeat it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you are a professional policeman, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I'm a police officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What kind of police work do you do? What is your speciality, so to speak? Do you work on the discovery of crimes or is it something else? You are a detective, if I understood what was said correctly.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. I've been a detective for over 18 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, how long did you stay in Yugoslavia altogether?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I went to Yugoslavia on the 6th of June last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: First time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: In Serbia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You returned?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. I've been back many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the question was: How long did your stay in Yugoslavia last?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I've been assigned to Yugoslavia from the 6th of June last year, and I remain assigned to Belgrade to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now I understand. So you've been in Belgrade for almost a year now; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During that year, have you had meetings with representatives of the authorities in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Which authorities do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. During your stay in Belgrade, were there any visits from the OTP, from the Office of the Prosecutor that you work for? Were there any visits paid by them to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in these meetings that the Prosecutors had with the representatives of the authorities when they travelled to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Are you referring to the visit made by the Prosecutor to Belgrade, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to her visit and to other visits of the representatives of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This witness has given evidence about exhumation, and your cross-examination should concentrate on that and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assume that I can ask him whether he took part in talks with the representatives of the authorities in the country that he went to to dig up corpses, that is. I do not see that that goes beyond the scope, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Only in relation to the exhumation. Mr. Fulton, help us with this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I didn't take part in any of the meetings with the Prosecutor that she had whenever she visits the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The statements that you gave and that are used today were given on two occasions. Where did you give your statements?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where did you make your statements, your witness statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And which investigator did you give your statements to?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It would have been to my team leader, Mr. Kevin Curtis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that the person who kidnapped me from Belgrade, Mr. May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. That's not a relevant question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that you were there to supervise the exhumations. What does "supervision" mean, the supervision you've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I never said that I supervised. I was there in a capacity to monitor. It was quite clear to me and made quite clear to me, as my role was non-interventionist, I had no influence, I offered no direction, I simply observed what was taking place by members of the Belgrade Institute of Forensic Science and other institutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So let me rephrase the question. What do you mean by "monitoring" now? I'm not asking you about supervision. I'm asking you about monitoring. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I observed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe all actions from when the team start -- teams started to work until they would finish their work? Did your working hours coincide with the working hours of the teams?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: For the first Batajnica site certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me whether it was established -- whether it was established at all and whether it was ultimately established when the bodies were brought to the locality where you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That question has to be answered by the officer conducting the investigation. I was not there in an investigating capacity, I was there purely as an observer. I cannot refer to how long the bodies were to be in the ground. That's simply within the purview of the forensic team and their area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you know nothing about this; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: About what, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: About when these bodies were brought to the locality where you had them dug up.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Indications that were throughout the press were that these bodies had been placed there during 1999, primarily April and May 1999. This was information that was given in informations to the press by the investigating police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So apart from information obtained from the press, you have no other information from the spot, from contacts with your people who were carrying out the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The people who were carrying out the exhumations were not my people. They were members of institutes from Serbia. It is up to them to make determinations regarding that matter, it's not up to me. I do not have the expertise, the knowledge, or the capability of doing that. I was there merely to observe and to monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the forensic part of the work here now. There is no doubt that forensics experts are experts in their own field. I asked you a different question. I asked you whether you had any other type of information, and you said no, you did not. Awhile ago, you gave answers to the Prosecutor's questions as to how you identified such-and-such a person and how you identified yet another person. You remember all of that. This was five minutes ago. You remember that she asked you about many persons, how you identified them. Now, was any person identified here at all, Mr. Fulton, and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There's been no formal identifications made to date. I did not say that these -- I said that these were identification documents that had been recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you heard the Prosecutor asking you how did you identify such-and-such a person, and how did you identify yet another person? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Several times she put her questions that way, how did you identify a particular person? Does this answer of yours now mean that you enumerated documents that were found in the ground amongst scattered clothes? Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was the witness's evidence. How the Prosecutor chooses to phrase her questions is not a matter for the witness. His evidence is this: That amongst the clothing found in these various graves with the bodies, there were these identifying documents. Now, that's his evidence. It's a matter for the Court to weigh.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. I think that what you said just now implies that he should answer my questions as well rather than give comments in relation to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So my question is: Were the bodies identified or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's answered that. No formal identification was made, but there were these identifying documents. That is the state of the evidence. Then those documents tie up, it's said, with missing persons. Now, the witness can't really take it very much further than that, and it will be for the Court to determine the probative value involved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why you're bothered by having the witness answer me whether these bodies were identified or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Because he's answered you. He said there was no formal identification, but he said there were these documents found. Now, he can't take it any further than that. He's a witness. He's telling us what happened, and that's what happened. Whether you want to argue that that doesn't identify anybody, that's a matter for you, and you can argue it in due course. But there's not good trying to argue with the witness. Well, it's time to adjourn, in any event. We'll adjourn now. Twenty minutes. Mr. Fulton, you'll remember, of course, not to speak to anybody about your evidence during the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, when I asked you whether you supervised the process of exhumation, you said no, and you explained that you never said that and that you were just an observer and monitored it. Now, I'm going to quote one or two passages from your statement, page 2, I think, and it says: "I am at the moment an investigator working for the OTP. I have been employed in this position since June 2001, when I was assigned to Belgrade to observe the exhumation process that was taking place within the boundaries of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word the accused is using in Serbian is "supervise."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: No. I observed. I monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That means that in the statement on this point, the -- it has not been -- what you were doing was not written correctly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Or not translated correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say in the English? I haven't got the English version in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't have it either, but -- Ms. Romano, have you got the English there? We now have the English. The second paragraph of that, the first page of the statement. "I was assigned to Belgrade to observe the exhumation process that was taking place."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My next question is the following: As you spoke about documents, was it ever established that these were authentic documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's a question I simply can't answer. That may well be up for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the investigating judge or the investigating judges, were they present at the exhumation process all the time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I don't believe so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the exhumations from the very beginning or did you join in at some later stage?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Batajnica 1 and 2 from the very beginning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you then describe to me how, before the exhumations began, what the sites looked like where the exhumations took place. What did the sites look like before the exhumations started?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: For Batajnica 1, I was not -- I was there after they'd done an exploratory clearance and dig to establish that there was -- or they believed the bodies to be there after the area having been pointed out by the investigating police officer. The second site at Batajnica, inside the SAJ camp, was a -- just a clear area with some small shrubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many people took part in the exhumation process, actually carried it out?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Those details are contained in the report of Professor Dunjic that's in the binder, the second binder. It lists everybody who was involved, and it will also list -- it will also explain what the area was like prior to clearance. This was his site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? That means that you know all the names of the people who carried out the exhumation, and they are listed in that report. Is that what you're saying? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And were there any photographs or video records of the sites before the exhumation started?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how was the digging done? What with?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It was done manually after an initial mechanical excavation. From then on, it was done manually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What depth were the bodily remains that you're talking about found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe those details should be contained in the forensic report. Those were not details that I was recording. I had no input into this exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in what state of decay were the bodies that you found -- that were found? What state of putrefaction?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I could only say what I see, and this will only be in layman's terms. The bodies were skeletal with some flesh. They were commingled. There were multiple fractures, either post or before death, I simply do not know. These are questions that should be answered by the forensic team and should be contained in their reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in the digging-up stage or the exhumation stage, was this recorded on videotape or photographs?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about the locations, the sites, which you say are BA1 and then you mention body BA09 -- that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What bodily remains were these? Was it a skeleton or were there still traces of tissue left on the corpse?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I know that there's a photograph of BA09 following exhumation. Perhaps that will answer the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
