I'm now showing you what has been marked in these proceedings as Exhibit 18. Do you see any photographs there which correspond to the uniforms that you saw in Racak on the 15th of January, 1999? Would you look at the photos, please.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: You're now looking at the television screen, but if you would look at the photographs to your left that are on the ELMO, and could you use the pointer and point out if any of the photographs in Exhibit 18 are the ones -- are like the ones you saw the individuals wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: May I start up? May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Please. Point on the photo itself and it will show on the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm not getting the screen. My screen is blank, so ... All right. Could you -- I'm sorry. You've done it, but I couldn't see what you were pointing to. Could you point to the uniforms again, please.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: You're pointing now to some individuals in photograph number 6 of Exhibit 18. Is that the uniforms like you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Are there any other uniforms that you saw that are shown on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Do you see any other photographs that bear a resemblance of the other uniforms you may have seen in Racak on the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Only those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Okay. You are also pointing now to the top right-hand one, number 4 on Exhibit 18; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The statement should be exhibited. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It will be handed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I believe there are two statements, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That will be exhibited as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement will be Prosecution Exhibit 174; the redacted version, 174A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have got questions for this witness, but before that, I wish to ask you why you made it impossible for me to refute the arguments put forth by the Prosecutor in relation to the previous witness, Kelly Barney, who left before he came in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You will have the opportunity on Thursday when we return to that argument. I said that we would hear argument on Thursday from everybody on that issue. So there are no -- no decisions have been made about his evidence. That is going to be dealt with on Thursday after we hear this witness and the general tomorrow. We will return then to Mr. Kelly. Now, let --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And as for Maisonneuve tomorrow, how come it is possible to give him only three hours when he is the only one who was in Racak on the 15th of January? We cross-examine and examine people here for three days, people who were not in Racak, whereas his time is restricted. What does this restriction mean? Does that mean that yet again I will not be in a position to have enough time to cross-examine him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will consider the position when we've heard his evidence. He has so far only made himself available tomorrow. We will have to consider what the position over all should be and whether it will be necessary for him to be recalled. But let's deal with this witness now and deal with him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A month ago, approximately, a documentary film was played on TV Pristina, and you appear there in a KLA uniform, together with Fadil Idrizi from Kosare; is that correct? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I can't answer that with a yes or no. I would have to give you more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just give us the detail. Tell us, first of all, whether it's right that you were on the television film, and then you can give an explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was never on television and was never a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mentioned that your father and your brothers were supporters of the party led by Hashim Thaci who founded that party after the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: My family, we all supported the party of Hashim Thaci, yes. Both parties, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were your father and brothers members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The KLA and the party of Hashim Thaci, did they have a local organisation in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the villagers were forced to join the organisation that was led by Hashim Thaci?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please? I don't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the villagers from the village were forced to join the organisation that was led by Hashim Thaci?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mentioned that the villagers helped dig trenches for the KLA for two or three months or, rather, two or three months before the events of the 15th of January, that they worked during the night and that your father and your brothers helped dig trenches. This is the last sentence in your statement on page 6 and the first sentence on page 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know what my father did. It was up in the mountains. I don't know, because I didn't see what he was doing up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am linking this to your statement, to what it says in your statement. What your statement says is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on whose instructions did the villagers start digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when did they start digging trenches? Can you give us the date more precisely when they started digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you do not know about what you spoke of in your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you help us with this: Your statement says: "My father and brother helped dig the trenches." Now, can you explain why that is in your statement if it's not true? Or it may be that it is true. Can you assist us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat that, please? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your statement says, page 7 of the English: "My father and brother helped dig trenches."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I know that they went up into the hills. Maybe they did dig trenches up there. But I didn't see what they was doing there. Maybe they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so I can continue then. And how many villagers worked on trench digging?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I didn't see them, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about the trenches in Racak. I'm not talking about trenches in the mountains. It's the trenches near Racak that are now being contested.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I didn't see them, and I don't know where they are, where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you in Racak at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When were you not in Racak? Could you please give us the date? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? It was when the war started in Kosova. We were refugees. There was no place safe in the village. There was nowhere we could find safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And from when until when were you not in Racak? You said a minute ago that you were not in Racak. From which date until which date were you not in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't remember the dates. I can't tell you because I don't remember. It was during the war in Racak. Everyone set off as refugees, and then we returned later in 1998. And we were refugees all the time. We were outside the village all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But in your statement, you mentioned that the villagers helped dig trenches for the KLA two or three months prior to the events of the 15th of January. That's what it says in your statement. Were you in Racak two or three months prior to the 15th of January or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't remember when they dug the ditches, the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when they were digging machine-gun nests?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You gave this statement on the 22nd of May, 1999, and then you did remember. Have you forgotten that since the 22nd of May that year or do you not remember at all? On the basis of what did you give your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I said I don't know because I wasn't there. I didn't do that work. I don't see why I have to repeat myself here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to repeat anything. I am asking you about the substance of your statement. You say in your statement that on the hill of Bebushit which you call Kodra e Bebushit, that is to say the place where the alleged massacre took place, there were some KLA soldiers up there. Now, is that correct or is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Which date are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the event. I'm talking about the event where the alleged massacre took place. And you said that there were KLA soldiers there. That's what you said in your statement. You know what you stated. Now, I ask you whether that is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown the statement in the Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Until she's shown it, may I move on to my next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 7 of the statement, you say that two months prior to the 15th of January the KLA was in the village of Racak for a month without interruption, that they had been there for a month without interruption. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Before the massacre on the 15th of January, I don't remember exactly, but I did see soldiers beforehand, four or five on the 4th or 5th. I don't remember how long they stayed. I did see them. They looked over the terrain. They weren't there all the time. They went off to their secret location then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in your statement, you say they were there for a month without interruption, all the time. Now you're saying something different. So which of the two is correct? Were they there for a month without interruption or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No, they weren't there for a month, were not there for a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what it says in your statement is not correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: It's true that they weren't there for very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that same page of your statement, you go on to say that one night, Serb soldiers and policemen entered Racak on foot and that the KLA prevented them from doing that and that two members of the KLA were wounded on the occasion. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: That's what I heard from the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many members of the KLA were in the village at the time when those two people were wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what you say in your statement you heard only from the villagers themselves; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: From the villagers I heard that two soldiers had been wounded, but I didn't see them myself. I just heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the people that you said you saw for a short space of time in the village, where were they?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't remember where they were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us more specifically, or at least roughly, the date when this took place?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any OSCE observers in the village at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many villagers from Racak had weapons at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I didn't go round from house to house to have a look at how many weapons they have. I don't know. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many did you see who were armed outside the houses?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I didn't see -- I never saw anyone with an arm in his hand, with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the ones you say you saw did not have weapons either. You saw them without weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: With the KLA members, was there a doctor there by the name of Vezir Bajrami from the village of Petrovo? And you mention him on page 7 of your statement, in the last line.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Vezir Bajrami is not from Petrova. He's a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And was he with members of the KLA in the village at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this clash between the police and KLA in which you said that two people were wounded, how many other clashes of that type took place in 1998? Do you happen to remember?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And as you say that when the war in Drenica broke out, do you know what was actually going on in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: How could I possibly know what was going on there? I was just concerned about my own neighbourhood. That's all I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now in view of the fact that you make mention of Drenica in your statement twice on page 4 and the conflicts in Drenica, who did you get that information from as to what was going on in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? Because I don't really understand what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was just following on from your last answer when you said you don't know anything about Drenica, and you mentioned Drenica in your statement. Now, as you mentioned Drenica and the clashes in Drenica twice in your statement, and it is on page 4 of your statement, my question to you is: Who did you get this information about what was going on in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the fairness of the witness, I would quote your statement in the written statements. You said: "When the war broke out in Drenica, the Serbian army and police were present on Pisha, Geshtenja, and Cesta hills. There was a big presence of them there with a lot more tanks, APCs and jeeps." You said this. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see -- in Cesta I saw the Serb police and military. There were tanks there and other equipment, and in Pisha too, and in Geshtenja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that what you heard from people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I saw them in Geshtenja and in Cesta. Not in Pisha itself, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the people that gave you this information about Drenica, were they the same ones who clashed with the police in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: The people didn't give me the information. I saw it on TV myself. And then I knew that the war had broken out in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah, I see. So you saw that on television, what you're claiming. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you're asking me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You just said you saw it on television. So you didn't see it personally. You saw it on television; right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: The Serb police and army, I saw them with my own eyes at the Cesta Hill, on the Cesta Hill, and on the Geshtenja Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But as you're talking about Drenica, does that mean that you knew what was going on in the municipality of Stimlje, which is your own municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know what happened. I can only tell you about my own village -- my neighbourhood, the part of my village where I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In your neighbourhood where your village is located near Racak, there's Mala Pojtsa [phoen], Petrovo, and Belince, and to the south and west of it. Do you know how many KLA members there were there and that from those areas they launched constant attacks on the police? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know, and I didn't see that there was shooting, that the army had shot there. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a compatriot of yours, that is to say, an Albanian, by the name of Xhemajl Bytyqi from Racak, who was a member of the local security force there, that is to say, the local police force? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you give me the name again? I didn't understand the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Bytyqi Xhemajl from Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No, I don't know him. I don't know such a name. I don't know him, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, and we're talking about this particular individual on the 18th of November, 1998, that the KLA set fire to his house? Did you hear about that, about that event? Because when a house is set fire to in a village, the villagers usually know about it. Do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: In the village of Racak, there was no KLA soldier whoever burnt a building with the exception of the 24th of August, 1998, when the Serb police and army gave orders and started burning the village. I'm not exactly sure how many village -- five or six houses, on the 24th of August, 1998, it was. The Serb police and army burnt our village. That was during the first offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know the Albanians named Xheladini Fehmi from Racak and Fatime Abazov, also from Racak? Do you know those people?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Fatime Abazov in December, at the end of December 1998, reported that four KLA members stormed their house and took Xheladini off only because he worked as a cleaning person in the police station? Do you know about this incident, that somebody who worked in the police station as a cleaner was taken off by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know another Albanian by the name of Shefsedin Ramo working in Elektro Kosmet? Do you know him? He's also from Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know him, no. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about Ramadani Halil, also from Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you ask the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Halil Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many inhabitants does Racak have? Tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: It could be about 300 houses, maybe more. I'm not exactly sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know a single one of the names I've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No, I don't know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 4, you say that you and your family took refuge in the cellar of a neighbour of yours that was called Hajrizi Shukri; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in that same statement, on that same page, you said that Hajrizi was arrested during the war because he had a cellar and he was held in prison for several months; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: That was during the first offensive in 1998, on the 24th of August. It was a Sunday when the Serb police and army entered our village, and I -- my family and I, we left --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So what you said is correct. Then you go on to say on page 5 --

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I can tell you, if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You state on page 5 that he was arrested by the paramilitary and that you personally know that it was the paramilitary that did this. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: It was the Serb police, yeah. Your paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you make a difference between the uniforms worn by the police, the army, the KLA, the paramilitaries? You're able to distinguish between all those uniforms, are you?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I know very well police and army -- Serb police and army uniforms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what kind of uniform did these paramilitaries wear whom you say arrested this person?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: The Serb paramilitaries were wearing camouflage clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how, then, do you say it was the paramilitaries and not the police or the army, if they had the same uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: The Serb paramilitaries had a scarf, a bandanna, and on their arms they had a distinctive sign, emblem. And their faces were blackened, were coloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these people who arrested this man were wearing bandannas or scarves on their heads; right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the people who arrested him had bandannas or scarves on their heads and that you were able to conclude on that basis that they were paramilitaries? They didn't wear caps of any kind, they had these bandannas?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Everyone in the village called them paramilitaries so that's what I called them. They -- they -- you could see from their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me this: Why would anybody be arrested for having a basement in his house? I assume that every house in Racak has a basement. Does it or doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know why the arrest was made. I know -- the whole family was together, the men, the women, everyone together. We went down to the basement, and they came, and they said, "Who owns this house?" They asked. The owner answered, and he said, "My name is Shukri Hajrizi, and they told him, they asked him, "Where is your brother Naser Hajrizi?" Naser Hajrizi was with the police before the war broke out in Kosova. He worked in Ferizaj and they fired him, and he was forced to go to Switzerland, and I don't know anything else, what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't clear on this point. That's why I'm asking you. And on page 4, you say that Hajrizi was arrested during the war because he had a basement, and I'm asking you why would anybody be arrested simply for having a basement in his house? Why a basement? How can that be a reason for anybody's arrest, having a basement?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: He had built the basement because of -- fortified the basement because of the shelling from the Serb forces, and we had to take refuge in there. That was his fortified basement. You know why he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah. So that was a sort of fortification and not just a basement.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: It was a basement but was -- it was -- it was remodelled because of the shelling. It was fortified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you show to Investigator Kelly which basement it was and what kind of basement it was?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes. Kelly took photographs of the place where we had been staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you showed him that fortified spot; right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which other details did you show Investigator Kelly apart from this fortified place? Which other details did you point out to him and show him?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I don't know what the question is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you said that you showed Investigator Kelly this fortified place, and I'm asking you now: What else did you show him when he talked to you? What else did you show Investigator Kelly?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: I showed him this basement, how we entered with the whole family. There were other families there too because the Serb police and army were shelling with all sorts of arms from Cesta and Geshtenja, they had been shelling. It was on a Sunday, on the 24th of August. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then you say that on the 15th of January, in the morning, at 7.00 a.m., you went to your uncle's place, Emini, Hysni Emini is his name, and that you spent the time there in his basement with another 45 people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: That was on the 15th of January, the day when the Serb police and army committed the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were in that basement with another 45 people, in the basement of your uncle's house; right?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how big is the house?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: It's a three-storey house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Three-storey, you say. And is there a fence of any kind round the house?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: We were in the basement, in the garage where the cars were. That's where we were staying, in the garage, the basement garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether there was a fence of any kind round the house.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: A normal house has something around it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, was it a concrete partition or made of wood? What kind of thing was it?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: When we were in the basement, we were lying on the floor. There was wood there in the basement, unvarnished wood. I don't know what you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about what was round the house. I'm asking you about how the house was encircled. You said that there was a fence or wall. Was it made of concrete or of wood? What was the house surrounded with?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: No. There was no fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the house had no fence or wall round it; right? Has it got a fence or wall or not?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Where we were in the basement there, where there was wood -- there was unvarnished wood all around, wood. There was lumber. And we were lying on the floor when they were -- the Serb police and army were shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now this hole in the wall, in the basement through which you were able to see, how far above ground was it? You say that you were able to look through it and see through it. How far above ground was this hole? And you talk about this on page 11, on the first line of your statement. You say you were walking from a hole in the basement, from an aperture in the basement.

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now you say you were lying on the floor. Were you lying down on the floor or were you watching through this hole?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: We were lying on the cement, on the cement floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. A moment ago you said that the floor was a wooden floor, but never mind. How, then, could you see the hill - what was its name? - Bebushit. How could you see that hill if you were lying down on the concrete floor?

utterances.speaker: DRITA EMINI
utterances.text: We could see the hills across from us from where we were staying in that basement. We could see the hills across from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The time has come when we must adjourn. Mr. Milosevic, you've had 40 minutes for your cross-examination to date. Twenty minutes outstanding. I'm now going to see when it's convenient for that to take place. Have we any further news about the general tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. General Maisonneuve is here. He is available all day tomorrow, has commitments, and would obviously appreciate being completed tomorrow morning, if possible, but if necessary, can make arrangements to return at a later date, much like General Drewienkiewicz did, for cross-examination, if absolutely necessary. But he cannot stay until Thursday. He has a 7.00 flight in the morning on Thursday, back for some urgent matters that he must attend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Then if it's not inconvenient, it may be better for this witness to come back on Thursday to conclude her evidence so we can get as much of the general done as possible tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That is very sensible, especially in light of the fact that we do have a reduced time period, starting at 10.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Emini, we have to adjourn now. There's 20 minutes or so left for your examination. Would you be kind enough to come back on Thursday morning, just to conclude that, at 9.00. Meanwhile, would you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Half past ten tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of May, 2002, at 10.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
